newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS, STEELERS, COLTS MOVE TO 5-1.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS, STEELERS, COLTS MOVE TO 5-1.

text.p: Gus Frerotte threw for 280 yards and two touchdowns and Henry Ellard caught eight passes, lifting the Washington Redskins to their fifth straight victory, 27-22 over the New England Patriots.

The Redskins (5-1), who share the NFL's best record, gave up 164 yards to Curtis Martin, whose two-yard TD run pulled the Pats within 24-22 with 5:33 to go. But Martin suffered a two-yard loss on a potential game-tying conversion run.
Drew Bledsoe was 23-of-48 for 222 yards for the Patriots (3-3), who had a three-game winning streak snapped.

But the day belonged to Frerotte, who drew praise from Skins head coach Norv Turner. "He's matured," Turner said. "You get a chance to play, and you're going to get better. He's had great presence in the pocket for a long time."

In Pittsburgh, Mike Tomczak's 32-yard touchdown pass to Kordell Stewart snapped a third-quarter tie and Jerome Bettis eclipsed 100 yards rushing for the fifth straight game as the Steelers posted a 20-10 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals.
Pittsburgh (5-1), which tied a team record with 10 sacks, including 4-1/2 by Chad Brown, has won five straight games.
"I've been putting pressure on myself because I only had one sack coming into this game," said Brown. "Today was definitely a coming out party for me."

In Indianapolis, Marshall Faulk and linebacker Jeff Herrod scored touchdowns 2:16 apart in the second half to boost the Colts (5-1) back into sole possession of the AFC East lead with a 26-21 victory over the Baltimore Ravens (2-4).
Herrod picked off a pass from Vinny Testaverde and rumbled 68 yards up the sideline for his second career TD.
Testaverde, who was 17-of-30 for 235 yards and one TD.
Jim Harbaugh threw a touchdown pass and Cary Blanchard kicked a pair of field goals for the Colts.

In Buffalo, Terrell Buckley snuffed a last-gasp drive by returning an interception 91 yards for a touchdown with 47 seconds remaining and the Miami Dolphins used dominant defence to defeat the Bills (4-2) 21-7.

The Dolphins (4-2), who broke a two-game skid, had seven sacks and four turnovers, despite starting four rookies on defence. Karim Abdul-Jabbar and Irving Spikes scored on short touchdown runs for Miami, which snapped an eight-game losing streak without Dan Marino as its starting quarterback.
Marino's sub Craig Erickson was 14-for-29 for 192 yards.
In Jacksonville, Nick Lowery joined the record books on a day his woeful New York Jets lost an 11-point lead and fell to 0-7 after a 21-17 loss to the Jaguars.
Lowery's 20-yard field goal in the fourth-quarter was the 374th in his career, moving him past Jan Stenerud as the NFL's all-time leader.
Mark Brunell threw a pair of touchdown passes for the Jaguars (2-5) who were outgained 367-289.
Frank Reich threw early touchdown passes to Adrian Murrell and Wayne Chrebet to give the Jets a 14-3 lead.

At Carolina, Kerry Collins threw three touchdown passes, including two to tight end Wesley Walls, and Kevin Greene returned a fumble 66 yards for a score as the Panthers (4-2) routed the hapless St. Louis Rams 45-13.
Collins also hit rookie Mushin Muhammad, making his first NFL start, with a 54-yard touchdown pass and Michael Bates ran 92 yards for the first kickoff-return score in club history.
Carolina's Anthony Johnson for a club-record 122 yards.

At Dallas, Emmitt Smith ran for 112 yards and two touchdowns, including the 100th rushing TD of his career, as the Cowboys (3-3) welcomed back wide receiver Michael Irvin with a 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals (2-4).
Irvin, back after missing five games for violating the NFL's drug-abuse policy, caught five passes for 51 yards.
"I would be lying if I wasn't worried about the crowd," Irvin said. "It was a warm welcome and I appreciate that."
In Atlanta, rookie Eddie George had his third 100-yard game and Al Del Greco kicked three field goals to lead the Houston Oilers (4-2) to a 23-13 victory over the 0-6 Falcons.
George carried 23 times for 109 yards for the Oilers who had one TD pass apiece from Chris Chandler and Steve McNair.
Bobby Hebert threw a pair of TD passes for Atlanta.

In New Orleans, Doug Brien's career-best 54-yard field goal with 1:44 remaining was the difference and Ray Zellars rushed for a career-high 174 yards as the Saints (2-5) recorded a 27-24 victory over the Chicago Bears (2-5).
Jim Everett completed 22-of-31 passes for 223 yards and two touchdowns for the Saints, but Dave Krieg was 19-for-28 for 247 yards and three touchdowns for the Bears.
At Tampa Bay, Trent Dilfer enjoyed his finest day as a pro, passing for 218 yards and three touchdowns and leading the Buccaneers (1-5) past the Minnesota Vikings 24-13.
Dilfer, who entered with the second-worst quarterback rating in the league, completed 22-of-35 passes, including two scoring strikes to Robb Thomas.
Robert Smith rushed for a career-high 133 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries for Minnesota (5-2).

At New York, Gary Anderson kicked a go-ahead 29-yard field goal with 2:12 remaining and William Thomas returned a fumble 23 yards for a touchdown on the next play from scrimmage to give the Philadelphia Eagles a 19-10 victory over the Giants.
Philadelphia's Ricky Watters rushed for 110 yards.
The Eagles (4-2) limited New York (2-4) to 150 total yards and just nine first downs.
Rookie Amani Toomer returned a punt 65 yards in the second quarter for the Giants' lone TD, which gave them a 10-3 lead.
In Oakland, Jeff Hostetler threw for 295 yards and four touchdowns, including two to James Jett, as the Raiders raced to a 34-point lead and defeated the Detroit Lions 37-21.
Hostetler completed 27-of-38 passes for Oakland (3-4).
Scott Mitchell threw three touchdown passes in an eight-minute span of the third quarter for the Lions (4-3).
